findings.title: New assignment_source kwarg passed to sync_assignee_outbound implementations that don't accept it
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue, user, assign=assign, assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` unconditionally. The abstract method signature in `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` was not updated (it still only declares `external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs` — and concrete implementations such as Jira and VSTS define `sync_assignee_outbound(self, external_issue, user, assign=True)` without `**kwargs`). For any integration whose override does not accept extra keyword arguments, every outbound assignee sync will now raise `TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'`, which will retry 5 times and permanently break assignee sync for that provider. All concrete overrides need to be updated to accept (or swallow) the new kwarg before this ships.

findings.title: Dataclass field default `queued=timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` calls `timezone.now()` when the class body is executed, so every `AssignmentSource` instance created without an explicit `queued` value shares the same timestamp frozen at module import. The intended 'when this was queued' semantics are broken (the value can be hours or days stale in a long-running worker). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead. The round-trip test does not catch this because it only asserts the key exists, not that it is fresh.

findings.title: queued datetime may not survive Celery serialization of assignment_source_dict
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which leaves `queued` as a `datetime` object, and this dict is passed directly as a Celery task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict`) in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. If the task serializer is JSON (the integrations queue commonly runs with JSON-serializable kwargs), enqueuing will fail with a non-serializable datetime, meaning no outbound assignee sync happens at all whenever an `assignment_source` is present. Either serialize `queued` to an ISO string in `to_dict` (and parse it in `from_dict`), or drop the field since nothing reads it.

findings.title: Sync-cycle guard only applies when parsed source survives; from_dict silently returns None on malformed payloads
findings.body: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` swallows `TypeError`/`ValueError` and returns `None`, and the task then calls `should_sync('outbound_assignee', None)`, which skips the same-integration check entirely. Any malformed or version-skewed payload in the queue (e.g. an older worker enqueued a dict without matching fields, or `queued` arrives as a string that later validation rejects) silently disables the cycle protection this PR adds, reintroducing the Jira assignment loop. At minimum a malformed payload should be logged; ideally an unparseable source should be treated conservatively rather than as 'no source'.
